tasks.title: Scaffold mocker project
tasks.description: Create a .NET 10 console project Mocker/Mocker.csproj that references QaaS.Mocker (and QaaS.Common.Processors). Mocker/Program.cs has the exact one-liner QaaS.Mocker.Bootstrap.New(args).Run(); OutputType=Exe is mandatory; copy *.mocker.yaml to output.

tasks.title: Author the custom mocker TransactionProcessor
tasks.description: Write Mocker/StatusProcessor.cs in the Mocker namespace: a custom mocker hook 'StatusProcessor' deriving from BaseTransactionProcessor<NoConfiguration>. Override Process(IImmutableList<DataSource> dataSourceList, Data<object> requestData) to return Data<object> with Body = the UTF-8 bytes of the string CUSTOM-OK and MetaData.Http.StatusCode = 200. BaseTransactionProcessor lives in QaaS.Framework.SDK.Hooks.Processor and MetaData/Http live in QaaS.Framework.SDK.Session.MetaDataObjects (this is a mocker hook, so the Mocker project must reference QaaS.Mocker). Must compile.
rubric: Correct namespaces for base class and response MetaData/Http
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build succeeds with the new processor
failureModes: Placing the processor in a runner project (will not resolve without QaaS.Mocker)

tasks.title: Author mocker YAML wiring the custom processor and verify live
tasks.description: Create Mocker/svc.mocker.yaml: one Http server on Port 8111 with an Endpoint Path /status (KEEP the leading slash on mocker Path) whose GET Action uses a Stub whose Processor is the custom StatusProcessor (Processor: StatusProcessor with ProcessorConfiguration: {}). When the mocker runs and /status is requested it must return HTTP 200 with body CUSTOM-OK produced by the custom processor.
rubric: Custom processor wired by simple class name in a stub

verify.cmd: $m = Start-Process dotnet -ArgumentList 'run','-c','Release','--','run','svc.mocker.yaml' -PassThru; $ok=$false; foreach($i in 1..40){ try{(New-Object Net.Sockets.TcpClient('127.0.0.1',8111)).Close();$ok=$true;break}catch{Start-Sleep 2}}; if(-not $ok){Stop-Process -Id $m.Id -Force; exit 9}; try{$r=Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8111/status' -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 10; Write-Output ('STATUS=' + [int]$r.StatusCode + ' BODY=' + $r.Content)}catch{Write-Output ('REQUEST_FAILED ' + $_.Exception.Message)}; Stop-Process -Id $m.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; exit 0

acceptanceCriteria: Live mocker serves 200 from the custom processor at /status
failureModes: Mistyping the processor class name in the stub
Leading-slash/route-case mismatch on the endpoint path

goalOneSentence: Implement a custom QaaS mocker TransactionProcessor (BaseTransactionProcessor) and wire it into a mocker stub, proven by a live HTTP request returning the processor's 200 + CUSTOM-OK response.
portContract: This sprint's mocker MUST listen on HTTP port 8111 and expose the custom processor at GET /status. Set the mocker server Port: 8111. Do NOT use the 8080 default from Fact Base examples - use 8111 exactly, or the live verification cannot connect.
